headline: Fed rate hike expected in September as Hormuz standoff drives inflation fears
tldr: US Bank forecasts a 25bps Fed rate hike in September; the rate-cut narrative is firmly dead after the FOMC held at 3.50–3.75%.
UK jobs slump is the worst since the financial crisis; postings fell 11% in H1 2026 and graduate vacancies hit a post-2020 low.
UK motor insurance market heading for a 108% combined ratio in 2026, with premiums forecast to rise 12% in 2027.
EY projects AI-related skills now appear in 9.4% of UK job ads, a record high, even as overall advertised wage growth slows to 3.9%.
Chancellor John Healey's first Budget is set for 28 October; BP has put its UK North Sea business up for sale ahead of it.

sections.title: Markets
sections.body:
**Markets — Thursday 6 August 2026**

The dominant macro backdrop remains the Strait of Hormuz standoff and what it means for oil and inflation. 
Core inflation and the Iran conflict's energy-price shock shifted market expectations from 2026 rate cuts toward possible rate hikes.
 
The FOMC held rates at 3.50–3.75% at its 29 July meeting,
 but 
US Bank now expects the Fed to raise by 25bps in September
 — the rate-cut narrative is firmly dead.

**US** — 
US stocks slipped as Treasury yields rose and investors digested earnings and labour data; the Dow fell 0.9% while the S&P 500 dropped 0.2% and the Nasdaq was off 0.1%.
 
The Dow was weighed down by a 3% drop in Salesforce after a leadership shuffle.
 
SpaceX tumbled 14% despite strong earnings as ~$101bn of shares became eligible for trading.
 On the plus side, your AMD (+1.50%) benefited from solid recent results, and ASML (+1.56%) tracked a broader AI-infrastructure rebound in Europe.

**Europe** — 
The STOXX 600 rose 0.3%, extending gains for a fourth session to a fresh record, led by Deutsche Telekom surging 6.3% after strong earnings and a raised buyback.
 
WPP surged nearly 24% on results that beat expectations.
 
The FTSE 100 slipped, diverging from the CAC 40 (+0.5%), with Bank of England rates holding firm keeping UK stocks on the back foot.


**Japan** — 
Tokyo opened flat around 66,300 with the yen still finding its level after rare coordinated US-Japan intervention.
 Your IJPN is essentially flat (+0.03%), reflecting that indecision.

**In your portfolio** — the modest gains in VUSA, VEVE, and WDEF sit in line with the mixed global tone. Rolls-Royce (+2.68%) and Chemring (+2.69%) are the standouts on the defence watchlist; BAE (-1.28%) is the laggard, likely on profit-taking after a strong recent run.

sections.title: Data & BI
sections.body:
**Power BI**

The July 2026 update is the most substantive in a while. 
Highlights include expanded modern visual defaults, conditional formatting for line charts and legends, model options in the Power BI Service, and TMDL View on the web.
 The TMDL View addition is practically significant — it brings tabular model scripting into the browser without needing Desktop. 
Measure descriptions can now be written via triple-slash comments directly in code
, which is a small but meaningful ergonomics win for documented semantic models.


From August, semantic model settings in the Power BI Service open in a new side pane rather than the full settings page.
 Worth noting for anyone with documented support workflows.


Visual calculations are now generally available, making it easier to add DAX calculations directly to a visual
 without cluttering the model. 
Users on Desktop versions from March 2026 or earlier will lose OneDrive/SharePoint save-and-share from October
 — update now if you haven't.

**BigQuery**


Continuous queries have reached general availability: any data written to a BigQuery table can now be pushed in real time to another table, a Pub/Sub topic, or Bigtable.
 This matters for near-real-time dashboards without a separate streaming stack.


An "optimised mode" for AI functions like `AI.CLASSIFY` trains task-specific models on the fly, delivering a 230× reduction in tokens consumed compared to row-by-row generative AI processing
 — relevant if you're running classification at scale inside the warehouse.

**Semantic layer**

The AI-agent pressure is reshaping how teams think about semantic layers. 
AI analytics failures are more often semantic failures than hallucinations — the model picks the wrong table, joins at the wrong grain, or aggregates incorrectly; a governed semantic layer prevents most of these errors before a query runs.
 
MetricFlow resolves metric names to SQL with grain validation, and invalid dimension combinations fail at compile time — a critical guardrail for AI agents that might otherwise invent joins.



The dbt Semantic Layer leans on dbt Cloud for the hosted layer and on the warehouse for execution, with no built-in pre-aggregation cache
 — teams with heavy concurrency or embedded use cases are increasingly evaluating Cube alongside it rather than instead of it.

sections.title: Career & Data Leadership
sections.body:
## 💼 Career & Data Leadership

**Market conditions: selective, not frozen.** 
Data analysts and AI engineers are holding up even in a slower market, because businesses continue to invest in automation and insight capabilities.
 
Demand for data professionals is up 7.7% year-on-year on new postings.
 That said, 
the UK job market is moving more deliberately — companies are still hiring, but with sharper criteria and longer pipelines.


**Salary benchmarks.** 
The projected average salary for data roles in the UK in 2026 is around £77,800, based on 2025 benchmarks plus expected annual pay growth of approximately 3%.
 At the senior/leadership end, 
salaries are rising 2–4% on average, with stronger growth of up to 6% across AI, data and cybersecurity.
 Worth noting for Milton Keynes: 
Edinburgh, Bristol and Cambridge are now offering salaries at 85–92% of London equivalents while commanding only 60–70% of London's living costs — often the best total-compensation ratio in the UK for senior professionals.


**Running the team: the mandate is shifting.** The clearest leadership signal right now is visibility, not platform-building. 
The defining risk for data leaders in 2026 is that technical credibility is no longer sufficient — the executives driving real impact lead the business *through* data, not just lead the data function.
 Practically, 
the most impactful data leaders treat organisational data literacy as part of their mandate — not training for its own sake, but targeted capability building that helps specific business leaders make specific decisions better.


**The governance bottleneck.** 
Without standardised KPIs and governed semantic layers, AI accelerates confusion instead of insight — analytics leaders should shift effort away from building more outputs and toward fixing the foundations those outputs depend on.
 
Organisations that treat data management as an afterthought will find their AI initiatives falter, while those who invest in high-quality, well-curated and accessible data will unlock superior outcomes.

sections.title: UK Insurance
sections.body:
**UK Insurance**

**FCA regulatory direction**


The FCA published the first of its new annual Regulatory Priorities reports for insurance in February, replacing the old portfolio letter format to communicate expectations more clearly.
 
The four stated priorities are: improving consumer understanding, claims handling and service quality; increasing access to insurance; ensuring fair value under Consumer Duty; and strengthening operational resilience.


On rule simplification, 
building on its December 2025 Policy Statement, the FCA is streamlining its Handbook — leaning more on Consumer Duty rather than product-specific rules — and will consult on simplifying GAP insurance rules, general insurance pricing data requirements, and information disclosure obligations.
 
Rule changes came into force in June and July 2026, per FCA Handbook Notice No. 142.


**Premium finance and access**


Premium finance remains under watch following the FCA's final market study report; while APRs have fallen since 2022, the regulator will continue to monitor and act where fair value concerns persist.
 
The FCA is also working with trade bodies and consumer groups to increase contents insurance uptake among social renters, and will independently review travel underwriting decisions affecting customers with pre-existing mental health conditions.


**Motor market: losses ahead**


EY forecasts the UK motor market will remain loss-making in 2026 and 2027; having slipped to a 102% NCR in 2025, EY now estimates a 108% NCR for this year.
 
The deterioration is driven by premium rate reductions feeding through to earned premium alongside persistent claims inflation; EY expects premiums to rise 4% in 2026 and a further 12% in 2027.
 The implication for Consumer Duty compliance is direct: repricing pressures must be balanced against demonstrating fair value.

**MGA/insurtech**


Insurtech UK launched a new Investor Network in June, aimed at connecting investors with start-up members.
 
UK insurtech Bertie launched earlier this year with an end-to-end MGA underwriting platform built around Lloyd's standards, with a single data-capture system designed to eliminate re-keying across submission, pricing, and policy issuance.

sections.body:
**Milton Keynes**

**Diary: MK Tech Week — 12–16 Oct**


MK Tech Week runs 12–16 October, culminating in a one-day conference and expo at Unity Place on **15 October**, where the focus will be on how the UK develops and protects critical technologies, data and digital infrastructure.
 
The theme is "Sovereign Technology" — covering the partnerships and innovations shaping the UK's future.
 Worth registering interest now; 
businesses, institutions and community groups can submit an event within the official programme at no cost.


**Diary: Powered Up Business Networking — tonight, 6 Aug**


Powered Up Business Networking runs this evening (Thursday 6 August, 7:30–9:30pm) at The Dolphin, Newport Pagnell — an informal, out-of-hours format that strips away networking formalities.
 
Tickets are £9.77.


**Diary: Code For Her meetup — 25 Aug; NatWest Tech Tuesdays — 25 Aug**


Code For Her (coding academy and forum for women) meets at Aiimi HQ on **25 August**, 18:30–20:30; NatWest Entrepreneur Accelerator runs Tech Tuesdays networking at the NatWest Community Hub on **25 August**, 11:30–13:00.


**Council & Infrastructure**


The council is investing over £6m in this year's road resurfacing programme; during August, 11 roads will be fully resurfaced.
 Expect localised closures — worth checking the council's interactive map before commuting.

The council itself is under new leadership following May's elections: 
no overall control, with the Lib Dems as the largest party and a Lib Dem–Labour alliance running the city under Cllr Jane Carr.


**Wider context**


UKRI has committed up to £20 million to The Open University-led Innovation Circuit project
, reinforcing MK's position within the Oxford–Cambridge Growth Corridor — relevant backdrop for anything you're watching on the data/AI skills pipeline locally.

I have gathered what verifiable, dated news I can from today (6 August 2026). The search results are thin on breaking stories specifically from today, but there are several confirmed, dated items I can work with responsibly. Here is the News section:

---

**🗞 News**

**UK**

- 
The UK is in its longest jobs slump since the financial crisis, according to PMI data
 — a backdrop that shapes the political pressure on the government heading into autumn. 
UK job postings declined 11% in the first half of 2026; graduate vacancies fell to their lowest level for this stage of the year since 2020, and advertised wage growth slowed to 3.9%, its weakest rate since early 2022.


- 
Demand for AI skills reached a record high, with AI-related tools mentioned in 9.4% of UK job advertisements
 — 
pointing to an increasingly divided labour market, where vacancies in software, engineering and IT have held up, while opportunities elsewhere have fallen sharply.


- 
Chancellor John Healey is set to deliver his first Budget on 28 October 2026.
 
BP has also put its UK North Sea business up for sale
, adding to energy sector uncertainty ahead of that fiscal event.

- 
Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband was urged by Marco Rubio to increase British defence spending during his first visit to Washington.


**World**

- 
FIFA said it had apologised for errors made over Gianni Infantino's failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup, with senior staff "reaffirming their full support" for his presidency
 at a crisis meeting in Morocco.

- 
An explosive device was found attached to a drone near the south runway at Leipzig/Halle Airport in Germany, discovered by an airport employee near a Ukrainian aircraft.
